gen_risks.description: ADISA and MIPA lack experience in executing large donor-funded operations, creating risks of implementation delays and non-compliance with World Bank fiduciary requirements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated Project Management Unit (PMU) within ADISA staffed with qualified financial, procurement, and administrative specialists, supported initially by the Ministry of Finance CFCU.
gen_risks.evidence: Neither MIPA, nor the recently constituted ADISA have previous experience in implementation of large donor funded operations

gen_risks.description: ADISA is a newly created agency without an established procurement track record, leading to a high procurement risk rating and potential contracting delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize the established CFCU under the Ministry of Finance during the PPF stage, hire experienced procurement specialists for the PMU, and prepare a detailed Project Operational Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: Since ADISA is a newly-created agency and the PMU is not yet fully set up, the procurement risk rating is high.

gen_risks.description: Substantial financial management risk due to unproven accounting and internal control systems across newly participating budgetary and non-budgetary entities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit two finance specialists for the PMU, procure dedicated accounting software, document financial management procedures in a Financial Management Manual, and utilize CFCU oversight initially.
gen_risks.evidence: The overall financial management risk is rated as Substantial.

gen_risks.description: Line ministries, agency heads, and field staff may resist ceding front-office customer service functions to ADISA or adapting legacy administrative workflows.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a structured change management and stakeholder outreach program, and leverage strong strategic coordination through the Inter-Ministerial Public Services Committee.
gen_risks.evidence: Ministries, agencies and individual civil servants may not welcome ceding the front office function to CSC. Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts to improve back-office functions.

gen_risks.description: Construction of the central Citizen Service Center (CSC) facility in Tirana generates localized environmental impacts including dust, noise, waste, and site safety risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate the World Bank OP 4.01 compliant Environmental Management Plan (EMP) into construction bidding documents, assign PMU oversight, and enforce contractor compliance.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential environmental impacts that are associated with new construction include dust and noise, waste generation, material supply, use of machinery on site

gen_risks.description: Focusing resources on high-end urban Citizen Service Centers and web-based e-services risks excluding poor, rural, elderly, and vulnerable populations who lack digital access.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain existing physical service access points, establish assisted digital access outreach centers in post offices/internet cafes, establish call centers, and track access indicators disaggregated by income and gender.
gen_risks.evidence: focus on state-of-the-art means for service delivery, such as online services or high-end urban CSCs, will diminish access of the poor and vulnerable

gen_risks.description: An overly compressed reform schedule across multiple phases creates risks of slippage in business process re-engineering, IT automation, and facility construction.
gen_risks.mitigation: Sequence implementation to deliver early wins via citizen feedback and performance monitoring while structuring loan disbursements around 5 key Results-Based Financing DLIs through 2020.
gen_risks.evidence: The Government’s timeline for the reform is very ambitious.

gen_risks.description: Achieving reform objectives across more than 10 government agencies involves complex inter-sectoral coordination that could lead to administrative bottlenecks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Empower the Prime Minister's Delivery Unit (DU) and the Inter-Ministerial Public Services Committee to actively track implementation progress, unblock institutional barriers, and enforce inter-agency cooperation.
gen_risks.evidence: Inter-sectoral reforms, especially those that involve more than a dozen government agencies, necessarily entail complex coordination.

gen_risks.description: Incomplete database archives, missing national ID numbers in key registries (e.g., property, transport), and legal disputes over ownership impair database interoperability and service automation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted technical assistance to digitize legacy records, populate unique ID numbers, optimize databases, and mandate connection to the NAIS Government Gateway interoperability platform.
gen_risks.evidence: The National ID number is missing for most records, only 45 to 50 percent of the archive is digitized, and legal issues over ownership remain

gen_risks.description: Process re-engineering requires enacting broad legislative amendments through omnibus legislation; parliamentary delays or legislative resistance could block necessary legal reforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Form specialized ministerial working groups to prepare legal inventories and re-engineering plans early, under the oversight of the Technical Inter-ministerial Committee.
gen_risks.evidence: Reform of government services and repeal of licenses, permits, and approvals will be implemented through omnibus legislation, expected to be passed by the end of 2016.

gen_risks.description: Modest national internet penetration (60%) limits direct citizen adoption of online transactional services (Level 3/4 automation).
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish physical CSC one-stop-shops and train post office, local government, and internet cafe staff to provide assisted internet access for online service delivery.
gen_risks.evidence: modest levels of internet penetration at only 60 internet users per 100 people in 2013

gen_risks.description: Implementing agencies lack sufficient technical personnel with expertise in software architecture, database management, and process re-engineering.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy US$5 million in Technical Assistance funding to hire specialized international and local technical experts to support NAIS, ADISA, and line agencies.
gen_risks.evidence: the authorities do not have staff with the technical skills and experience needed to implement the reform process.

gen_risks.description: High upfront capital investments and ongoing software licensing, operation, and maintenance costs for CSC and IT platforms could strain government fiscal resources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Explore public-private partnership (PPP) financing options for CSC construction/operation and capture budget savings from front-office efficiency gains and process re-engineering.
gen_risks.evidence: There are significant upfront financial costs associated with the development of the CSC, business process reengineering, digitization, automation, training staff and educating citizens

gen_risks.description: Discrepancies between official internal agency processing metrics and actual citizen experience obscure real service delivery delays and impede accurate performance management.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy proactive text-message (SMS) and phone-based Citizen Feedback Mechanisms (CFM) alongside periodic independent third-party user surveys to validate administrative tracking data.
gen_risks.evidence: The data submitted by the IPRO office on the other hand routinely records that almost all applications are processed within the required six days.

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity poses challenges to delivering the reform effort, despite very high leadership commitment and fast-paced GoA initiation of reforms.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project Preparation Facility (PPF) is designed to assist capacity building for the implementing agency; the TA part of the loan continues building capacity to deliver, addressing the most pressing capacity needs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risks related to the new form of financial instrument used in Albania.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the fiduciary risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk, named alongside the fiduciary risk as being addressed by the same TA support (fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU); not separately elaborated beyond this.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the technical design risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Stakeholder risks arising from inter-agency coordination.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by strong emphasis on coordination mechanisms in the design of the operation.

gt_risks.description: Bureaucratic resistance to enhanced transparency and simplification of administrative processes.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated in part through high-level leadership and engagement, and through citizen feedback arrangements that help pinpoint poor performance and corruption.

gt_risks.description: Political cycle risk from elections coming up in 2017, which could disrupt reform continuity and government commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by making early progress in showing results and ensuring a broad constituency of support for the project's objectives and activities among the leadership of participating institutions and service users.
